LESSON: HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.2: Historical Development of Agriculture
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Historical Development of Agriculture, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why did people start practising agriculture in Africa? 2. How did Agriculture begin in Africa?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. locate areas where early agriculture was practised in selected geographical regions in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Historical Development of Agriculture in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Historical Development of Agriculture together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: Learners are able to complete tasks as they carry out research in groups on animals kept and types of crops

which were grown during early agriculture in Egypt, Nubia and in Rift valley of the Eastern African region.

Values:
● Unity: Learners apply equity as they carry out research on animals kept and types of crops which were grown during early

agriculture.

● Patriotism: Learners develop citizenship as they discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to world civilization.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Social Cohesion: Learners classify crops grown and animals which were kept during early agriculture.

● Environmental Education: Learners illustrate methods of irrigation which were used during early agriculture.

Link to other learning areas:

● Learners use knowledge of animal husbandry as they research on animals kept and types of crops which were grown during

early agriculture in Egypt, Nubia and in Rift valley of the Eastern African region.

● Learners use creative skills as they draw diagrams showing methods of irrigation which were used during early agriculture in

Egypt.
